theory.intro: **Brokerage** is the fee charged by a broker to execute a share trade. Brokerage is added to the base cost when buying shares, and subtracted from the proceeds when selling shares.
facts: $\text{Base Trade Value} = \text{Market Price per Share} \times \text{Number of Shares}$.
Brokerage can be a flat fee or a percentage of the total trade value.
steps: Calculate the base value: $\text{Market Price} \times \text{Number of Shares}$.
Calculate the brokerage fee (percentage of base value, or flat fee).
Add brokerage to base value when buying shares.
Subtract brokerage from base value when selling shares.

Subtract total buying cost from net selling proceeds to find profit. For profit as a percentage of the cost of the shares, divide the profit by the buying share cost before brokerage and multiply by $100\%$.

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) Buy $375$ shares at $\$8.62$ each with a flat brokerage fee of $\$31$. Find the total cost.
(b) Sell $640$ shares at $\$5.47$ each with a flat brokerage fee of $\$29$. Find the total income.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Share cost $=375\times8.62=\$3232.50$.
Total cost $=3232.50+31=\$3263.50$.
(b) Share income $=640\times5.47=\$3500.80$.
Total income $=3500.80-29=\$3471.80$.
Add the fee when buying; subtract it when selling.

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) Buy $725$ shares at $\$6.84$ each with $1.4\%$ brokerage.
(b) Sell $920$ shares at $\$7.36$ each with $1.8\%$ brokerage.
Find the total cost in (a) and total income in (b), to the nearest cent.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Share cost $=725\times6.84=\$4959$.
Brokerage $=0.014\times4959=\$69.426$.
Total cost $=4959+69.426\approx\$5028.43$.
(b) Share income $=920\times7.36=\$6771.20$.
Brokerage $=0.018\times6771.20=\$121.8816$.
Total income $=6771.20-121.8816\approx\$6649.32$.
Keep the original values until rounding the final amount.

Tipeni bought $300$ shares in a company for $\$22.00$ each and paid $\$35$ brokerage.
He sold them two years later for $\$28.00$ each and paid $\$35$ brokerage.
What is his profit as a percentage of the cost of the shares before brokerage, correct to $2$ decimal places?
development.solution_text:
$\text{Share cost}=300\times22=\$6600$
$\text{Total buying cost}=6600+35=\$6635$
$\text{Share income}=300\times28=\$8400$
$\text{Net proceeds}=8400-35=\$8365$
$\text{Profit}=8365-6635=\$1730$
$\text{Percentage profit}=\frac{1730}{6600}\times100\%$
$\approx26.21\%$
